transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time... I guess I'm here because things have been a little intense lately. 

I mean, I was barely settling into my new apartment, and then I just... I don't know, I got really motivated, I guess? I started saying yes to all these mentoring sessions, and I took on extra client prototypes for work. I'm a web designer, by the way. And on top of that, I suddenly decided I needed to redesign my whole portfolio. 

It was like I had to fix my entire life in one giant sprint, if that makes sense? I mean, being productive is a good thing, right? But I guess it just got to be a bit much all at once, and... well, I just wanted to make sure I'm handling things okay. Is it alright that I came in for that?
Have you been feeling unusually happy or excited lately?

Um, yeah, I guess you could say that. Earlier this month, I felt... really upbeat? Almost electric, actually, which was great for getting all that work done. 

But, um... I don't know if this is the right way to explain it, and I feel a little embarrassed even admitting this, because I really try to be an easy person to work with... but I also got a little... on edge? Like, one minute I'd be super excited and happy, and the next I... well, I kind of snapped at a contractor. And my sister, too. Just over these tiny, tiny delays. It honestly felt like they were personally trying to block me from finishing things, which sounds so silly out loud. 

I felt awful about it right after. I'm not usually like that, I promise. Is it normal to get a little snappy like that when you're just really focused and excited about a project?
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?

Um, well, my sleep has been... maybe just a little off? But I'm sure it's just normal stress from all the projects, you know? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining. 

It's just that lately, I... well, I either lie awake in bed just kind of replaying everything I messed up that day—which I know is silly, I really try to focus on the positive and not dwell on things. Or, um, I'll wake up super early, like around four in the morning when the traffic outside starts, and I just can't get my brain to quiet down again after that. 

I mean, a lot of busy people have trouble sleeping, right? It's probably nothing major. I hope that answers your question okay... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you had trouble concentrating on tasks lately?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think I've actually been pretty focused? Especially with all the redesigns and the mentoring. I was just kind of locked in, you know? 

I guess... well, maybe when I was feeling more down, like when I couldn't sleep, my brain would feel a little foggy the next day. But that's just because I was tired, right? Anybody would be a little distracted if they were up at four in the morning. When I'm actually working, I feel like I'm doing a good job staying on track. I hope that makes sense? I really try to be diligent about my work.
Do you often feel guilty or self-critical about the things you've said or done when you're feeling down or after you've snapped at someone?

Um, yeah... I do. I mean, I know everyone feels bad when they mess up, right? I try really hard to be conscientious and treat people well. But... well, especially lately, when I get in one of those slumps, I just get so incredibly hard on myself. 

I'm a little embarrassed to even admit the things I think about, honestly. I just... I keep telling myself that I completely ruined the separation, and that I've just wasted so much money. And with my design work, I'll convince myself I've completely disappointed my clients, even if they haven't said anything. It's like... I don't know, it just feels like I somehow make every practical problem worse just by being me? 

Which I know probably sounds so dramatic, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around throwing a pity party. I try to stay positive, I really do. I just... I hope it's okay that I'm sharing that. Is it normal to be that hard on yourself sometimes?
Have you had a period of time, say a few days or more, where you felt consistently elevated or unusually happy, without the mood swings you mentioned?

Um... consistently happy? I don't know if I'd say it was completely consistent. I mean, earlier this month, I definitely had a stretch where I felt really... almost electric, I guess? Just incredibly upbeat and energized about everything. 

But, um... I did still have some swings, I think. I'm actually a little ashamed of this, because I really pride myself on being professional and easy to get along with, but... one minute I'd be in that amazing mood, and the next I kind of... well, I snapped at one of my contractors. And my sister, too. 

It was just over these tiny little delays, nothing major at all, but in the moment, it felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done? Which I know is totally unreasonable of me, and I felt terrible about it after. I really try not to treat people that way. Does... does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples.
Did you have any days during that upbeat period where you didn't snap at anyone or feel irritable at all?

Um, well... I guess if I really think about it, no, not completely. I mean, I really wish I could say yes, because I hate being that kind of person. But even on the days where I felt really, really good—like that electric, upbeat feeling I mentioned—there was always this... edge to it, I guess? 

Like, I'd be having a great morning, getting so much done, and then suddenly I'm just so impatient. That's when I'd snap at my sister or the contractor. It was like they were moving in slow motion and I just couldn't handle it. I really didn't mean to be harsh, I just... I wanted everything to keep moving at the same pace I was. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound awful. I really do try to be patient with people. Is it normal for those two feelings to happen on the same day like that?
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Um, well... I really try to keep up with my hobbies, because I know how important it is to have balance, right? But... I guess lately, if I'm being completely honest, it's been a little harder to get into them. 

I used to really look forward to going hiking at Crowders, or, you know, cooking something nice for myself. Even just sketching out interface ideas for fun, outside of work. But recently... I don't know, I just kind of stare at my hiking gear or my tablet and... I just don't feel that same pull toward it? 

I know I should probably push myself more, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just being lazy or giving up on things. I just... I haven't had the same spark for it. I hope it's okay that I haven't been keeping up with all of that as much as I should. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
Did your upbeat and energetic feelings come and go throughout the day, or were they steady for most of the day?

Um, well, the... the upbeat feeling, the electric kind of energy I was telling you about? It was mostly steady for the whole day, I think. Like, I'd wake up feeling just incredibly driven and positive. 

But then, um... like I mentioned before, the irritability would just sort of spike in the middle of it. So I'd be having this great, productive day, and then... I'd just snap at my sister or the contractor over those little delays. It wasn't that the good feeling went away, exactly, it just... it got kind of sharp and impatient? 

I really hate admitting that, because I want to be someone who stays calm and positive all day. I try so hard to be easy to work with. But yeah, the energy was there most of the day, just... sometimes it came out as me being too harsh when I felt like people were blocking me from getting things done. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you been experiencing these mood swings and energy levels for most of the past month?

Um, well... yeah, I guess so. It feels like it's been about that long. 

Since I moved into my new apartment, which was, um, about a month ago... that's really when this whole intense up-and-down pattern started. I mean, I try to keep things steady, I really do, but ever since the move, it's just been this rollercoaster of feeling so incredibly productive and then... crashing, or getting so irritable. 

I know moving is supposed to be stressful, and I've been trying to just handle it well and not let it get to me. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses for being all over the place. Is it pretty common for a move to trigger something like this for a whole month?
Did you ever feel so good or high that you didn't need to sleep at all?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say I didn't need to sleep *at all*. I know how important rest is, and I really try to maintain a healthy sleep schedule, I promise. 

But, um... there was a stretch of a few nights where I... I guess I only slept maybe three or four hours? But the thing is, I didn't feel exhausted or anything! I woke up feeling completely fine, actually. I just figured, well, if I'm awake and feeling good, I should probably just use the extra time to get ahead on my design work, you know? 

I didn't want to just lie there if I had the energy to be productive. I hope that doesn't sound too unhealthy... I really was just trying to make the most of my time. Is it normal to feel that okay on so little sleep sometimes?
Did you experience both the upbeat, energetic feelings and the irritability or depressed feelings almost simultaneously, rather than one after the other?

Um, no, I don't think they happened exactly at the same time. It wasn't like a mix of both all at once. 

Usually, I'd have the really good, energetic feeling going strong, and then... well, then the irritability would kind of just flare up, like I mentioned. Or I'd have the crash and feel down later on. But they felt pretty separate, if that makes sense? 

I really hope I'm not being confusing. I try to pay attention to my moods so I can give you the right answers, but sometimes it's a little hard to sort out. Does that sound like what you were asking?
Did you ever feel like you were able to function normally or even exceptionally well during periods of reduced sleep?

Um, yeah, I guess I did function pretty well. I mean, I actually got a lot done during those few days when I wasn't sleeping much. 

I was working on this new interface for a client, and the ideas were just flowing so easily. I felt really sharp, honestly. I was turning around wireframes faster than usual, and the client was really happy with the progress. So, I definitely wasn't, like, falling apart or making mistakes because of the lack of sleep. 

I really try to keep my work quality high, no matter what. I hope it's okay that I just leaned into it and got the work done? I figured as long as I was being productive and not messing anything up, it wasn't a big deal to just keep going. Is that a bad thing, to be able to work like that on less sleep?
Have you ever felt both extremely happy and irritable at the same time, rather than one after the other?

Um, well, I think we just talked about that a little bit, right? I really don't think they happened at the exact same time. 

I know it sounds like it could be a bad thing if they were all mixed together, but I really don't feel like I was ever out of control like that. Like I said, I'd feel really great and productive, and then maybe get a little irritable later on if things got in my way, but it wasn't this big confusing jumble of both all at once. 

I try really hard to keep my emotions separate and manageable, you know? I hope I'm answering this right... I just don't think I've ever had them happen simultaneously like that. Is it okay that they were separate?
Have you ever felt both extremely happy and depressed at the same time?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I think that's kind of similar to what you were asking before, right? 

When I'm feeling really happy and productive, that's just... that's all I feel. I'm just in a really good mood. The depressed feelings, the times when I'm feeling really down and sluggish, those happen at completely different times. It's never a mix of both. 

I'd never want to sound like I'm completely all over the place emotionally. I really try to keep things grounded. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful by clarifying that they definitely don't happen together.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely happy or irritable and also had increased energy or activity that lasted for at least one week?

Um, a whole week? Well, I guess... I mean, this whole pattern, the up-and-down thing, it's been happening since I moved into my new apartment about a month ago. 

But I wouldn't say it was a full, unbroken week of just being extremely happy or irritable. It's more like... a few days here and there where I'm just really energized and getting the apartment set up and working on my designs. I mean, a whole week sounds a bit extreme, right? I definitely try to make sure I'm taking breaks and not pushing myself too hard for that long. 

I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. It's been going on for a month, but it's not like I was bouncing off the walls for seven days straight. I really try to keep things manageable. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Did you have at least four consecutive days where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had increased energy?

Um, four days... yeah, I think maybe I did? I mean, when I was getting everything unpacked and set up, there was a stretch where I was just really focused and felt super good about everything. 

I guess it could have been four days in a row where I just had a lot of energy and was really on top of things. But it wasn't a bad thing, you know? I was just being really productive and getting my life organized. It didn't feel like I was doing anything wrong or acting strange. 

I hope it's okay that I felt that way for a few days. I just really wanted to get my place looking nice. Does that sound like what you're asking about? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can.
Have you had two weeks or more where you consistently felt depressed or down?

Um, yeah... I guess I have. I mean, I really try not to dwell on things, and I try to stay as positive as I can, but... 

The heavier stretches of feeling down, they've actually been showing up since my separation. That was about 11 months ago. So even before this latest move to the new apartment made everything feel a bit sharper, I'd have these periods that lasted a couple of weeks where I just felt really low. 

But I figure that's a pretty normal reaction, right? To be sad for a few weeks after separating from someone? I really don't want you to think I'm just letting myself fall apart or anything. I always try to push through it and keep working. I hope it's understandable that I'd be depressed for a couple of weeks under those circumstances. Does that answer what you were looking for?
Did you have at least four consecutive days where you felt extremely happy or had increased energy without any significant breaks in between?

Um, yeah, I suppose for those four days earlier this month, there weren't really any breaks in that energy. I just felt... almost electric, you know? Like, really upbeat and just going, going, going. 

But, um... I guess it wasn't just happy energy the whole time. I feel a little embarrassed to admit this, because I really pride myself on being polite and easy to work with, but... I did get a bit irritable. One minute I'd be super upbeat, and the next I kind of snapped at a contractor. And my sister, too. It was just over these tiny delays with the apartment, but right then, it felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done. 

I always feel terrible when I lose my patience like that. I really don't want you to think I'm a mean or angry person. I was just so wired and focused on getting my designs set up... it's pretty normal to get a little short-tempered when you're that invested and energized, isn't it? I hope that makes sense and answers your question.
Have you felt depressed or down for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

Um, yeah, I guess I have. I mean, I really try to put on a brave face, especially for work and for my family, but... lately, it's just been there almost all day, every day. 

I wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling in my chest. And I try to shake it off, I really do. But even when the apartment is totally quiet and nothing bad is actually happening, I just feel so overwhelmed. Like, I feel like I could just burst into tears over something as silly as a coffee mug left in the sink. 

I feel so bad admitting that, because I know I should be stronger and handling things better. It sounds so dramatic, crying over a mug, right? I really hope you don't think I'm just being weak or feeling sorry for myself. I'm trying my best to push through it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
